chapter: Arranging, Fletcher Henderson and Lucky Millinder
title: Hoping to replace Henderson on piano; Charlie Christian and Benny Goodman
summary: He copied for Henderson only briefly, hoped to be a pianist in the band, and Charlie Christian planned to introduce him to Goodman but died; Alphonso Trent is mentioned.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Right. It seemed to me there were --(yes, well it -- even that you'd done arrangements for Jimmy Dorsey's band and did you actually arrange for Fletcher's band too?

No, no. I only copied music for Fletcher Henderson for a brief time while he was in town, and the band was at the Coconut Grove. In fact I was trying -- I was hoping that I'd be able to replace him a sa pianist, because as an arranger he wasn't considered to be a very, you know, flowery pianist who was flattering the band. I think Johnny Guarneri had been in the band, who has an excellent pianist, one of my favorites today. But Fletcher was not real-ly loose enough to be a jazz piano player. And Charlie Christian, who then was with Benny Goodman and a friend of mine from the old days in Oklahoma City when I travelled with Nat Towles, was going to try to recommend me to Benny Goodman and get me a shot, an of audition.
But unfortunately Charlie died before he got a chance to introduce me to Benny Goodman and --
Teddy was with him then though, wasn't he? Or Jess Stacey was with him too.
No, I think Teddy Wilson had left. See Teddy had left --
You know, Lionel and Teddy had left him.
See, this is -- you know, the later period, like around -- this was, I don't know, in the forties some time.
You know, just to go back a minute. You mentioned about Nat Towles. Yes, well Charlie was in that for a time, wasn't he, with Nat Towles' band. Charlie Christian was for a time.
He played with another band. I can't think of the name, in that neighborhood in Oklahoma. He was from Oklahoma City. There was another band, Alphonso Trent.
